text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a ~25% tokens/sec drop in prod since the canary rollout at 09:05 UTC. CTB queue depth rising, latency tail increasing. Reverting? cc @derek @simo
ci-bot: perf-alert: perf-e2e job shows +22% p99 latency on scheduler tests. https://ci.redwood/tests/9876 (tagged perf-regression)
derek: On it. what's the rollout commit/PR? grabbing dashboards now.
maya: Rollout was release/v1.13.2, PR #4321 (scheduler: prefetch/window-adjust). Merge commit: 5a7b9f. Notable: KV cache hit dropped 87% -> 63% on canary nodes.
simo: Did a quick bisect locally — suspicious commit is 5a7b9f. It changed prefetch window and batch coalescer heuristics. Ran `git bisect` across builds, output:```# bad: 5a7b9f (merge) # good: 4c2d11 (previous) first bad commit: 5a7b9f commit 5a7b9f - scheduler: adjust prefetch window```
alex: Profiled a canary replica (perf samples): heavy stacks in `coalescer::wait_for_window`, and elevated `memcpy` activity during kernel selection. Sample snippet:
```
#0 coalescer::wait_for_window
#1 scheduler::assemble_batch
#2 kernel_selector::choose_for_batch (small_batch_path)
#3 cuda_memcpy_async
```
nora: Also seeing avg tokens/batch drop ~18% post-merge. Small batches trigger the small-batch kernel execution path which has higher per-token overhead.
derek: KV logs show a spike in misses around the rollout time:```[2026-03-18T09:05:23Z] kvcache.lookup miss key="prefetch:seq:12345" count=1``` Looks like key generation or prefetch ordering changed.
simo: Reproduced locally with a canary image built from 5a7b9f: enabling the previous prefetch heuristic restores KV hitrate and tokens/sec. Suggest hold and revert PR #4321.
maya: Putting the rollout on HOLD. @deploybot please start a revert for canaries.
deploybot: rollback-request acknowledged. initiating rollback for canary group (r-8791). ETA ~6m.
ci-bot: Note: perf-e2e that runs on canaries earlier failed on the merged build (5a7b9f) — median tokens/sec down ~20%. Logged under PR #4321.
alex: Action items: 1) revert PR and monitor metrics 2) add a perf test exercising long-tail sequence distribution and assert tokens/sec + kv hitrate 3) add unit test to kernel selector to avoid unexpected small-batch path flips 4) add probe in CTB to expose batch-size distribution in CI.
nora: Filed PERF-913: "CTB warmup + prefetch regression after scheduler prefetch change". Assigned to eng-runtime, attaching repro script and perf traces.
derek: Any objections to immediate revert? If none I'll approve the revert PR.
simo: No objections, +1 from me.
maya: Revert PR opened: #4332 — reverts commit 5a7b9f. CI will run perf job after merge.
ci-bot: queued perf job on post-merge images; results expected in ~15m.
deploybot: rollback complete on canaries (r-8791). health checks passing. Monitor tokens/sec for 30m.
maya: Monitoring dashboard shows tokens/sec back to baseline on canaries; KV hitrate recovered to ~86%. Good sign.
derek: Keep thread open for postmortem notes. We'll upload perf artifacts, allocation maps, and the mini-repro to PERF-913.
alex: Also follow-up: evaluate if kernel-selection thresholding should consider transient drops in avg batch size (warmup jitter) before flipping kernels.
nora: Adding that to PERF-913 checklist. closing the hold when postmortem and CI guards are in place. :thumbsup:
